set.approach: Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Coondoggolin splits the middle of the south face by its prominent crack.

Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Coonstock is on the left side of the south face; it crosses a few horizontal cracks on face holds before entering a widening crack that leans right.

Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Racoon sits at the right end of the east face; face moves lead to a crack that opens up slowly.

Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Star Gazers is on the right side of the south face, going past horizontal cracks and flakes.

The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. Acme Crack takes the southwest arete of the southernmost formation.

The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. Dorada climbs the northeast arete of the southernmost feature, starting from a small podium near two bolts.

The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. Pleasant View Arete follows the southwest arete of the southern formation.

The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. The route starts in the notch between the two formations, around the corner and up-left of Cattlestar Faticus, reached by easy class 2 ground with minimal brush, and climbs the southwest face of the higher formation.
Natural Resources Rock lies directly southwest of High Profile Pinnacle and very close to the road. Jungle Fever starts a few steps left of Natural Resources, up a lieback crack.

review.notes: Area + route; shares a finish but descent not stated for this route.

set.approach: Natural Resources Rock lies directly southwest of High Profile Pinnacle and very close to the road. Walk around behind the formation from the road and descend to roughly beneath the summit block. Start in the middle of the west face, on the first inviting crack just left of the summit.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor on top of the summit block.

review.notes: Route page: rap anchor on top.

set.approach: Park at the hairpin turn; the trail heads north from the bend. It crests a small rise, drops to cross a seasonal stream, then switchbacks uphill to The Coven at the base of Dragonlance Wall, the first wall reached. Dobby's Dungeon starts behind a large pine, left of Squeal Like A Pig and close to the right of the gully used to reach Voodoo Wall.

From Emerald Bay, take the trail to Eagle Lake and get across its outlet. Work along the lakeshore, then swing up and to the right toward the foot of a big gully full of talus, whose right side is a tall rock wall. Climb the gully until it flattens into a benched area with views of the Velma Lakes, cross the bench while keeping the buttress in sight, and where the bench bends away, weave up the slabs on the right to an obvious ridge that leads to the base. This route is on the small crag at the foot of the northeast face of Eagle Lake Buttress. It climbs the blunt southeast arete; look for the right-leaning splitter crack with a small left-facing offset.
set.descent_text: Build a gear anchor at the top and walk off.

review.notes: Route page: gear anchor, walk off.

set.approach: From Emerald Bay, take the trail to Eagle Lake and get across its outlet. Work along the lakeshore, then swing up and to the right toward the foot of a big gully full of talus, whose right side is a tall rock wall. Climb the gully until it flattens into a benched area with views of the Velma Lakes, cross the bench while keeping the buttress in sight, and where the bench bends away, weave up the slabs on the right to an obvious ridge that leads to the base. This route is on the small crag at the foot of the northeast face of Eagle Lake Buttress. It takes the zigzag crack in the center of the east face, which is identified by a clear horizontal crack low on the face.
set.descent_text: Build a gear anchor on the nuts or cams at the top and walk off.

review.notes: Route page: gear anchor, walk off.
